What should the back button mean in kolu?

Analysis·seedling·proposed·JUL 16, 2026

Today one physical button has two unrelated meanings chosen by mouse position: over a Code-tab preview it steps the file browser; anywhere else it walks browser history (until DL2's fix, a stack of stale deep-link teleports). The decision: one meaning, which one?

Contents

  • The bug (fixed in DL2)
  • The design question — one button, two meanings

Found live by srid while dogfooding DL2 (#1864): click a deep link to a terminal, press mouse-back, land somewhere unrelated. Root cause split in two — one bug (fixed), one design question (this note).

The bug (fixed in DL2)

Deep-link routing pushed a browser-history entry per link while ordinary navigation recorded nothing, so the history stack was a list of stale teleport commands; back replayed the previous link, not the previous place. Fixed by reflecting external hashes via history.replaceState — the URL stays durable and copyable, but links never push entries.

The design question — one button, two meanings

  • Pointer over a Code-tab preview: the sandbox traps mouse X1/X2; the in-iframe SDK forwards them and kolu drives the file browser’s own back/forward — back means “previous previewed file”. A deliberate feature (artifact-sdk/client/bridge.ts — “so the buttons behave the same over a preview as over the file tree”).
  • Pointer anywhere else: the browser’s real back — which, post-fix, walks whatever history the browser has (usually: out of kolu).

Two meanings selected by hover position is the confusion to kill. The options:

  1. Back = browser back, everywhere. Drop the preview’s X1/X2 capture; the file browser keeps its own visible back/forward buttons in the Code-tab chrome. Cheapest; loses the (genuinely nice) mouse-back-over-preview flow.
  2. Back = app history (“where I actually was”), everywhere — a real DL3. Ordinary navigation (terminal focus, host switch, panel/file changes) writes history too, so back/forward walk your real path through kolu. Needs a definition of a placeCandidate: {host, terminal, right-panel tab + file} — exactly the state the deep-link grammar can already express, which is what makes this DL3-shaped: every place is a deep link, and back/forward walk deep links you actually visited. and touches every navigation site; the view-only law is preserved (history entries mirror state, never mutate it).
  3. Keep the split, but make it visible — status-line hint while hovering a preview. Recorded for honesty; weakest option.

Recommendation: option 2 as the DL3 plan (the place-is-a-deep-link framing makes it small and principled), with option 1 acceptable as an interim if DL3 doesn’t get scheduled. srid rules.
